item.title: Sweden's defence plan must survive an America that leaves
item.description: Even with the Americans in, Sweden's Army and Air Force miss NATO's capability targets. A defence built on forces no Swedish minister controls is not a plan, it is a bet.

item.title: Kremlin tells Witkoff and Kushner Russia is ready to redesign European security now
item.description: The Kremlin says it wants European support for a new security architecture, yet keeps European envoys out of the Ukraine talks. Moscow and Kyiv also disagree on whether a ceasefire or a continental settlement comes first.

item.title: Zelenskyy gives EU until November to decide who speaks for Europe in war-end talks
item.description: Politico reports EU leaders meeting in Dublin are split among candidates for the role, while the Washington Post says Russia has resisted any European place at the table.

item.title: Europe must pay for the army Moscow wants bargained away
item.description: While Bulgaria and Slovakia refuse the package, the size of Europe's second-largest army on the continent is being settled in Abu Dhabi without us. Fund it now, every state contributing, or lose the seat at the table.

item.title: Europe has decided to leave Palantir. It has not yet built what comes next.
item.description: Spain, the United Kingdom and Germany have moved to end their dependence on Palantir, while NATO still runs the Palantir-derived system it chose when no European alternative existed. The Bundeswehr is testing about thirty European candidates, but no replacement is in service: sovereignty on this layer is a decision taken, not a capacity confirmed.

item.title: EU leaders to debate single envoy for Ukraine talks as Kushner presses Europe
item.description: Kushner said on 11 November that Europe should name one representative, and the question now goes to the informal summit in Dublin this week. Some capitals resist Kallas as too critical of Russia to sit across the table.

item.title: US Treasury Secretary Bessent moves to military base over Iranian death threats
item.description: Iran has warned Europe that any part in the US blockade of its economy will be treated as an act of war, and US refuelling tankers have been diverted from RAF Mildenhall in England. Prosecutors have charged three men accused of acting for Iran in a plot against RAF Fairford.

item.title: France blames Iran's Revolutionary Guard cyber unit for October attack, plans sanctions
item.description: Paris says the operation against French refrigeration systems was unprecedented in scale, and chief prosecutor Laure Beccuau is seeking international arrest warrants. ENISA warns its planned doubling of resources would never be enough.

item.title: Garda call Dublin summit security operation largest in state's history
item.description: Mark Rutte joins up to 50 European leaders for the ninth European Political Community summit as officials brace for hoax threats and cyber attacks.

item.title: Rutte says Spain and Portugal treat Ukraine war as a distant Polish concern
item.description: The NATO Secretary General said a Russian missile takes five minutes longer to reach Lisbon than Warsaw. Portugal's foreign ministry, led by Paulo Rangel, called the remark light treatment of a serious matter.

item.title: A sanction Russia can shop around is not a sanction, it is a leak
item.description: The Court of Auditors found that enforcement varies by capital and companies pick the weakest border. The EU pays the full cost of the embargo and delivers only part of the pressure, so enforcement must move to Brussels.

item.title: Turla planted a mail-collecting tool on a NATO state's Microsoft email server
item.description: Romania's state email ran on Microsoft servers outside European control while a Turla tool collected NATO- and EU-related messages, and a second Romanian system was found compromised weeks later. Government mail must move to European-run servers, and that decision belongs in the next budget cycle.

item.title: Europeans shut out of Ukraine-Russia talks as US brokers Abu Dhabi negotiations
item.description: Russian and Ukrainian teams held a second day of Kushner-brokered talks while European delegates held separate consultations, with Lavrov rejecting a ceasefire. Moscow wants Ukraine to cede roughly 2,000 square miles of Donetsk and Luhansk it failed to conquer.

item.title: US soldier at Nato HQ in England arrested on suspicion of spying for Russia
item.description: The 41-year-old, detained near Gloucester under the National Security Act 2023, was posted at Imjin Barracks, home of Nato's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps. He faces possible charges from both British authorities and the US Army, which can carry life imprisonment.

item.title: Italy to offer Ukraine access to two military radar satellites
item.description: Defence Minister Guido Crosetto takes the thirteenth aid package to the Copasir committee on 10 November, as Washington limits its own satellite support to Kyiv.

item.title: Moscow bars Europe from US-mediated Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Kushner and Witkoff mediate the first direct negotiations since February, as EU leaders decide this week who speaks for Europe. European security advisers remain outside the room.

item.title: Russia denies Europe a seat at Abu Dhabi talks set by Washington without it
item.description: According to Politico and Euronews, the EU will send officials to parts of the negotiations, but Moscow says no agreement allows it, and the format was agreed by Russia, Ukraine and the United States alone. Kaja Kallas has said the EU will not implement any deal it is not party to.

item.title: At least 20 dead off Crete as minister says Libya deal no longer holds
item.description: Shipping Minister Sevi Voloudaki says cooperation with eastern Libya has broken down and warns of stricter measures if the EU's return-hub initiative fails within days. Frontex aircraft spotted two further boats south of Crete, with roughly 47 and approximately 40 people aboard.

item.title: Nvidia board opens inquiry into whether Huang was targeted by foreign intelligence
item.description: The board says it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised. Three House chairmen have demanded a closed-door briefing on Chinese access to US chip technology by November 18.

item.title: EU and Canada launch Alliance for the Future as Canada joins EU defence procurement scheme
item.description: Canada becomes the first non-European participant in the EU's Safe scheme and has won contracts to supply Poland and Latvia, though the EU stopped short of the associate membership Von der Leyen had promised.

item.title: Kallas says Europe will refuse to implement any Ukraine deal it did not join
item.description: Washington and Moscow keep negotiating in formats with no seat for Europe, while Meloni asks the December summit to pick a single negotiator. Kallas said any agreement must stop Russia using a pause to rearm.

item.title: Congress moves to impeach Hegseth as Trump defends his secretary over Iran war
item.description: Representative Thomas Massie is preparing to force a vote on impeachment. Republicans had knives out after a $47 billion Iran war the Washington Post says doomed the party.

item.title: Iraq proposes regional ministers' committee as oil losses pass $60bn in US-Iran war
item.description: Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein says the committee would visit Tehran and Washington to seek calm. Iraq has lost $60bn, about €54 billion, since Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz, which carries 90 percent of its oil exports.

item.title: Belgrade court detains police commander over garage torture case
item.description: Belgrade judges ordered SAJ commander Igor Žmirić held for up to 30 days with eight other suspects, while bar association president Vladimir Prijovic says the timing of arrests raises suspicion that police and prosecutors serve political ends.

item.title: Commission puts mandatory migration solidarity to the Council's decision
item.description: The Solidarity Pool for 2027 would let member states pay €20,000 per person not relocated, but contributions bind only once the Council agrees, and Hungary and Slovakia pledged nothing for 2026.

item.title: Nordic defence firms call for joint missile warning and Arctic intelligence
item.description: Six companies behind the Nordic Compass Defence Statement ask the five governments to join a shared space-based missile warning system. Industry says budgets alone will not deliver capability without an integrated Nordic defence market.

item.title: Bomb threats hit dozens of European flights and force Irish newsrooms to evacuate
item.description: Italy's anti-terrorism prosecutors now coordinate investigations in four cities, as Spain's foreign minister calls the campaign an attempt at hybrid aggression and Dublin judges it probably coordinated.

item.title: Netherlands buys American drone software without competition and keeps parliament out
item.description: The defence ministry awarded an Anduril-linked contract worth 3,050,000 euros through a negotiated procedure, citing crisis urgency, and did not inform parliament; Follow the Money revealed the deal.

item.title: Russia strikes Zaporizhzhia aid point after Kyiv virtually ran out of interceptors
item.description: Zelensky says the death toll could approach 100 after the double-tap attack on Komyshuvakha, the deadliest strike on the region since the full-scale invasion. Latvia has called an extraordinary UN Security Council meeting.

item.title: Meta, Google and TikTok sue to block California's ban on addictive feeds for minors
item.description: The companies filed separate First Amendment challenges to Assembly Bill 1709 and asked a federal court to stop Attorney General Rob Bonta enforcing the law, which takes effect in January 2027.
